questions.topic: Late Interaction: ColBERT Token-Level Matching and PLAID Serving
questions.question: What does ColBERT store for each document?
options: One small vector per token, computed offline
A single pooled vector for the whole document
One scalar weight for each vocabulary term
A joint encoding of the query-document pair

questions.topic: Late Interaction: ColBERT Token-Level Matching and PLAID Serving
questions.question: How does ColBERT score a query against a document?
options: It takes the cosine between the two [CLS] vectors
It takes the dot product of two sparse vectors
It sums each query token's best document-token match
It runs a linear head over the concatenated pair

questions.topic: Late Interaction: ColBERT Token-Level Matching and PLAID Serving
questions.question: Why is ColBERT described as late interaction?
options: It reranks only after BM25 has produced its own list
Each side is encoded alone and they meet only at scoring
It defers all indexing until the first query arrives
It is trained after the cross-encoder teacher is trained

questions.topic: Late Interaction: ColBERT Token-Level Matching and PLAID Serving
questions.question: A 200-token document stored at 128 dimensions per token in 2-byte values costs about how much space?
options: About 1.5 KB
About 6 KB
About 13 KB
About 51 KB

questions.topic: Late Interaction: ColBERT Token-Level Matching and PLAID Serving
questions.question: How does PLAID make ColBERT serving fast at corpus scale?
options: It caches the top results for queries that repeat often
It converts every token vector into a BM25 impact weight
It recalls by centroid, then runs MaxSim on a shortlist
It swaps MaxSim for one document-level dot product

questions.topic: Late Interaction: ColBERT Token-Level Matching and PLAID Serving
questions.question: Which team should prefer ColBERT over single-vector dense retrieval?
options: One that wants token-level explanations and can pay in storage
One that needs the smallest possible index footprint it can get
One that has no accelerator available at ingest time
One whose queries never repeat vocabulary across sessions

questions.question: What is the training signal in cross-encoder distillation?
options: Thumbs-up feedback harvested from production logs
The teacher's own scores on query-document pairs
The student's own scores from earlier checkpoints
Random labels balanced across the relevance classes

questions.question: Why do soft teacher scores teach better than hard relevance labels?
options: They need far fewer training queries to converge well
They remove the need for a held-out validation set
They take much less disk space to store and reload
They grade the distance between nearly relevant negatives

questions.question: Why does distillation make economic sense for serving?
options: The teacher is paid for once offline and the student serves
The teacher model costs nothing at all to run once training ends
The student needs no evaluation pass once it is trained
Distillation removes the index rebuild from the lifecycle

questions.question: How can a team adapt its ranker to a new domain with no human relevance judgments?
options: Train the teacher on randomly paired domain documents
Distill teacher scores on unlabeled domain queries
Skip adaptation, since bi-encoders are domain neutral
Fine-tune the student on labels invented from BM25 ranks

questions.question: A distilled bi-encoder reproduces its teacher's blind spot on product codes. Why does this happen?
options: The student carries far too many parameters to generalize
Product codes change far too often for any index to track
The teacher's systematic errors became training targets
The vector index was built with the wrong distance metric

questions.question: Why is distilling a distilled model into an even smaller one usually a mistake?
options: Small students cannot consume soft labels during training at all
A grand-student needs far more training data to converge
The original teacher's license forbids a second transfer
Each generation compounds error and widens the capacity gap
